title: Weak-Key Key-Recovery Improvement for Speck-128
summary: For Speck-128, existing weak-key key-recovery attacks probably do not beat exhaustive search over the reduced key space; it remains unresolved whether cheap condition checks can yield a key-recovery improvement and, if so, what time...

formal_statement.body: For $\mathrm{Speck\text{-}128}$, existing weak-key key-recovery attacks probably do not outperform exhaustive search over the reduced key space, so only a distinguisher is reported. Determine whether the weak-key conditions can be checked cheaply enough---when candidate-key checking dominates the cost---to obtain a key-recovery improvement over exhaustive search, and provide a detailed analysis of the resulting time complexity.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptanalysis of Speck-128 in the fixed-key model, focusing on weak-key key-recovery attack complexity.
parameters: Weak-key conditions: conditions tested during key recovery
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether, when candidate-key checking dominates the cost, weak-key conditions can be checked cheaply enough to obtain a key-recovery improvement over exhaustive search, and analyze the resulting time complexity.

citations.label: Differential Cryptanalysis in the Fixed-Key Model

progress.summary: The source reports that its Speck-128 analysis probably does not improve weak-key key recovery over exhaustive search and therefore lists only a distinguisher. It leaves a possible improvement conditional on comparatively cheap weak-key testing and notes that detailed time-complexity analysis was outside the paper's scope.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., Differential Cryptanalysis in the Fixed-Key Model
